text:
alex (marketing): Quick ask for launch benchmarks — need a small focused rerun of the gen + embed flows for the press pack. Low-lift: prioritize reproducibility over breadth.

maria (marketing): main asks: p50/p90/p95 for gen (short prompts ~40 tokens + long prompts ~1k tokens), embed avg/99, coldstart heatmap (0-300s) and a sample of raw traces. Also quantized fp16/int8 comparison if doable.

devin (eng-runtime): Got it. Couple clarifying q's: 1) How many samples per cohort? 2) Which model variants exactly (open/quantized/custom kernels)? 3) Do you need end-to-end including network time or just server-side token latency?

alex (marketing): 1) 200 samples per cohort is fine for the deck. 2) Primary: redwood-1.2 (fp16), plus redwood-1.2-8q (quantized) — only if quantized path is already smoke-tested. 3) Prefer server-side only (so we can call out runtime wins separately).

maria (marketing): For prompts: a) short chat-like customer support comps (~30-60 tokens). b) long completion tail (~800-1200 tokens) — include a warmup prefix for long cases. Also one embedding payload (single sentence and paragraph).

devin (eng-runtime): Ok. We'll do gen short, gen long (with 1 warmup request per worker), and embed single vs paragraph. For long-case warmup: is a single repeated warmup request per worker sufficient or do you want a timed warmup (e.g., 30s)?

alex (marketing): Single repeated warmup per worker is fine. Document it in the artifact. Acceptance: p95 for long-gen should be within 1.5x of fp16 baseline for quantized to be considered "close enough" for marketing claims.

sam (eng-runtime): FYI quantized kernel for 8q still shows ~10% variance on tail depending on sequence tokenization. We'll include stderr bands in the artifact. Also can run isolated kernel-only traces if you want microprofiling.

maria (marketing): Please include the raw CSVs + a small README with exact commands so we can reproduce in postmortem. We may reference numbers in PR, need provenance.

devin (eng-runtime): Cool. I'll kick off a smoke rerun this afternoon. Using bench job:```bash
bench run --job launch-pack-2026 --model redwood-1.2 --variants fp16,8q --cohorts short,long,embed --samples 200 --warmup 1 --server-side-only --collect traces,heatmap,csv```

benchbot: Scheduled bench job 1789991234-1. Estimated runtime 2.5h. You'll get artifacts at: s3://bench-artifacts/launch-pack-1789991234/ once complete.

alex (marketing): Amazing — thanks. Can you also tag a snapshot for the press deck with the run id and include a short note if anything was noisy/failed?

sam (eng-runtime): Will do. If we see >5% p95 regression in quantized vs fp16 we'll attach a note and include a fallback messaging suggestion (e.g., use fp16 for low-latency tiers).

maria (marketing): Also tiny UX ask: include a single plot of "coldstart heatmap" with time buckets on the x-axis and counts on y — helps the narrative.

devin (eng-runtime): We'll produce the CSV + a pre-rendered PNG for that. Any specific color palette?

alex (marketing): No strict palette, but keep it accessible and high contrast (dark line on light bg).

sam (eng-runtime): Noted. Kicking off now, will post status and the S3 link when done.

benchbot: Job 1789991234-1 started on pool gpu-prod-5. Logs: https://logs.redwood.ai/1789991234-1

devin (eng-runtime): ETA ~2.5h, ping me if you need interim numbers.

alex (marketing): If we can get interim p95 for short-gen within 30m that'd be super helpful for the deck teardown.

sam (eng-runtime): I'll extract quick aggregates after the first cohort completes and post here.

maria (marketing): Thanks team! Feel free to @alex or @maria with any blockers. :rocket:

alex (marketing): Appreciated.

benchbot: Job 1789991234-1 completed. Artifacts: s3://bench-artifacts/launch-pack-1789991234/ — summary attached.

devin (eng-runtime): Quick post-run notes: short-gen p95 = 112ms (fp16) vs 130ms (8q) — within your 1.5x threshold. long-gen p95 = 1.9s (fp16) vs 2.3s (8q). Embedding mean = 18ms (sentence) / 48ms (paragraph). Raw CSVs and PNG heatmap uploaded.

sam (eng-runtime): Attached a tiny README: run command, model git hash, kernel versions, config JSON, and known caveats (tokenization sensitivity on quantized path).

alex (marketing): This is great — can we mark the run as "press-ready"? If yes, we'll proceed with claim drafting.

devin (eng-runtime): From runtime side this is clean. Recommend a short caveat: "Quantized variants may exhibit modest tail variance depending on tokenization and sequence shapes."

maria (marketing): We'll include that language. Thanks everyone, moving to drafting. :sparkles:
